patch_description:
This crossover combines the modular, well-documented block-construction style of the second seed (which achieved the best test accuracy 0.90 and lowest validation/test loss thanks to its rich set of entanglers: nearest-neighbor ring, skip-2, skip-3 and diameter connections) with the entangling-gate diversity of the first seed (which alternated CRZ and CRY on its skip-connections, giving richer non-commuting mixing at the same parameter cost).

Key design choices:
1. Per-qubit RY then RX rotation layers give full single-qubit expressivity (16 params/block).
2. A nearest-neighbor ring of CRZ gates with two alternating shared parameters gives local entanglement at minimal parameter cost (2 params/block), as in both seeds.
3. The skip-2 entangling layer now alternates CRZ and CRY (instead of being purely CRZ as in the second seed), directly reusing the winning idea from the first seed that mixing rotation axes on the entangling gates increases expressivity without adding parameters (2 params/block).
4. A skip-3 layer (single shared CRZ parameter) fills in the previously-missing distance-3 connectivity, as introduced in the second seed.
5. A diameter (distance N/2) CRZ layer gives one global, all-to-half-way connection with a single shared parameter, providing long-range mixing cheaply.
6. The whole block is applied twice with identical parameter names (weight-tying across depth), doubling the effective circuit depth/expressivity while keeping the parameter count fixed — the same "shared-depth" trick that drove the accuracy gains in both seeds.

This gives only 22 unique parameters (11 rotation/skip families x 2 not counted correctly — actually 8 RY + 2 ring + 8 RX + 2 skip2 + 1 skip3 + 1 diam = 22), a large reduction versus the 122-146 params of the seeds, which should improve parameter efficiency and convergence speed while retaining the entangling richness (ring + skip2 + skip3 + diameter, mixed CRZ/CRY) that produced the strongest validation/test performance in the prior generation.
